doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

chapter: Advice and becoming a jazz player
title: Why not piano: tendonitis, hearing Mingus and turning to jazz
summary: Rebellious adolescence, classical piano and tendonitis, hearing Mingus in San Francisco led to flute, soprano sax and learning jazz in record stores.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Why didn’t you become a jazz pianist?

I had more — I had tendonitis and — yeah and I was studying classical piano and I had a very — a rebellious adolescence. I went to five high schools getting kicked out of a few of them. And I really loved art and my last year, I guess it was in an art school and I thought I wanted to paint. And I always thought I want to do this, I want to do that. And I finally got serious about piano and I went at it a little too vigorously and I developed tendonitis and then I had to take time off from the piano. I did finally get my Grade Ten Piano Studies which was a big deal for me. But then I realized you know I was not going to be in that forum. I was not going to be a classical piano player. Everything — it was not. So I went to San Francisco and heard Mingus and when I came back from that trip, I heard him over like five nights. When I came back from that trip I decided I really

wanted to play jazz. And I bought a flute around that time and started kind of like tinkering around on the flute. And then friends from school just on the weekends somebody would be playing, you know a couple of guitars and a bass player and we’d just be jamming on two chord things. And I don’t know what we were playing. But anyway and I would play the flute too but I really didn’t know what I was doing, but having a great time doing it. And so then I just sort of transitioned then. I started to put the things together. Coming back from San Francisco I remember telling Don, because he was in the shows in San Francisco that I thought all the — I thought Mingus’s band was all classical musicians. I thought they were all studied classical musicians. I didn’t — you know I didn’t realize that there were different skills to do that kind of thing than there is to playing — I’m sure, Don was a classical piano player and he said he thought that was hilarious when I told him that. But yeah, so I transitioned and then I just started like by hanging out in record stores and pulling a record, “Who’s this guy Charlie Parker? Can you put this on?” And then being humiliated by the guy, “You don’t know Charlie Parker?” Yeah, I remember having the Joni Mitchell record with [sings] “My analyst told me.”

Yeah. Hendricks and Ross, Annie Ross. And I remember saying, “Wow I really love this record, Joni Mitchell sings like “My analyst told me” and the two guys that ran the store just looked at me like they just wanted to toss me out the place.

“Don’t you know?” And they went over to the thing and like held up a Hendricks and Ross — Lambert, Hendricks & Ross record and so there was a lot of humiliation in going through the steps. But all these people were — like I was willing to learn and they were willing to put records on and so I just went at it like that next. That’s how I sort of transitioned. I still love to play piano but you know if I sit at the piano for too long working on something my wrists are achy.
